pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Walk me through your Dockerfile: what does each stage do, and what exactly crosses from the first stage into the final image?
expected_points: each FROM starts a fresh stage; only the last one becomes the shipped image
the build stage has the toolchain and compiles the binary
COPY --from=<stage> lifts only the binary across; nothing else travels
earlier stages are still built and cached, they are just not kept

questions.prompt: Why does a Go binary need `CGO_ENABLED=0` to run on `scratch`? What is actually different about the binary?
expected_points: with cgo on, net and os/user use C implementations and the binary is dynamically linked against libc
a dynamically linked binary names a program interpreter (/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) that scratch does not contain
the failure looks like 'exec …: no such file or directory' about a file that exists — the missing file is the loader
CGO_ENABLED=0 links statically with pure-Go DNS and user lookup, so the binary needs nothing outside itself

questions.prompt: You picked a final base image. Defend it against the other two — what did you gain and what did you give up?
expected_points: scratch is empty: no CA certificates, no tzdata, no /etc/passwd, no shell — each is your problem to solve
distroless static adds exactly those (certs, tzdata, nonroot uid 65532, /tmp) and still has no shell; :debug exists
alpine gives a shell and apk at ~8 MB but uses musl, which bites the moment cgo is on
the trade-off is debuggability and convenience against size and attack surface

questions.prompt: Why do you copy `go.mod`/`go.sum` and run `go mod download` before copying your source? What happens if you don't?
expected_points: a layer's cache is reused only if its inputs are unchanged, and invalidating one layer invalidates every later layer
COPY . . changes on any source edit, so a combined step re-downloads every dependency on every edit
manifests change rarely, source changes constantly — order instructions rarest-changing first
after the split, a source edit rebuilds only the build step

questions.prompt: The naive image is ~900 MB and yours is ~10 MB. Where did the difference go, and why is the size a real cost rather than untidiness?
expected_points: the toolchain, the stdlib source tree, and a full Debian userland never came across
the compiled binary already contains the parts of the stdlib it uses
cost: pull time on every node and deploy, cold starts, registry storage, and CVE surface to scan and patch
you cannot delete weight later — a RUN rm in a later layer only adds a whiteout

questions.prompt: Why `USER 65532:65532` rather than `USER app`, and why bother with a non-root user inside a container at all?
expected_points: container uid 0 is host uid 0 unless a user namespace remaps it — defense in depth
a name needs /etc/passwd, which scratch does not have, so it fails at startup
numeric uids are what orchestrators can verify
non-root cannot bind ports below 1024, which is why the service listens on 8080

questions.prompt: What do `-ldflags="-s -w"` and `-trimpath` each do, and what do you lose by using them?
expected_points: -w drops DWARF debug info and -s drops the symbol table, typically a quarter of the binary
delve and nm no longer work on the shipped artifact; panic traces still do
-trimpath removes local filesystem paths, making builds reproducible and keeping your paths out of production
-X sets a string variable at link time, which is how version stamping works
